PulseBrief's Afternoon Pulse


Tue, Jul 14, 05:00 → Tue, Jul 14, 11:00


Cyber Security


SAP NetWeaver Critical Flaw (CVSS 9.9) Enables Memory Corruption — July Patch Day Drops 16 Notes


Jul 14, 24:00


SAP's July 2026 Patch Day includes a fix for CVE-2026-44747, a memory corruption vulnerability in SAP NetWeaver Application Server ABAP scoring 9.9 out of 10 on CVSS — the highest possible severity tier. The flaw affects multiple SAP kernel versions widely deployed across enterprise environments. With 16 security notes total in this release, any organization running SAP infrastructure should treat this as an emergency patching cycle.


A CVSS 9.9 flaw in the world's most widely deployed enterprise ERP platform is as close to a mandatory emergency patch as exists in enterprise security.


Sources: Cybersecurity News


Critical ServiceNow Sandbox Escape Allows Unauthenticated RCE — Affects Hosted and Self-Hosted Deployments


Jul 14, 24:00


ServiceNow disclosed CVE-2026-6875, a critical sandbox escape vulnerability in its AI Platform that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary code in affected environments. Both hosted ServiceNow instances and self-hosted deployments are affected. The combination of zero-authentication requirement and broad enterprise deployment makes this a high-priority remediation target.


An unauthenticated RCE in a platform running core IT workflows for thousands of enterprises is a top-tier patching priority — check your ServiceNow version immediately.


Sources: Cybersecurity News


Microsoft Entra ID Switches Default Authentication to Passkeys September 1 — Phishable SMS/Voice MFA Retired


Jul 14, 24:00


Microsoft will replace SMS and voice-based MFA as the default authentication method in Microsoft Entra ID with passkeys starting September 1, 2026. The decision is directly driven by Microsoft Threat Intelligence observing AI-enabled phishing campaigns achieving click-through rates of up to 54%, compared to roughly 12% for traditional phishing. Organizations that haven't planned the transition have approximately six weeks to act.


A platform-level authentication default change affecting every Entra ID tenant is a mandatory operational item for identity and access teams — the September 1 deadline is not soft.


Sources: Cybersecurity News


ShinyHunters Spent a Year Walking Into Salesforce Environments via OAuth Trust — Microsoft Maps Three Attack Paths


Jul 14, 24:00


Microsoft's threat intelligence team documented how actors matching ShinyHunters' TTPs have spent a year compromising corporate Salesforce environments without exploiting any Salesforce vulnerabilities, instead weaponizing the OAuth trust relationships organizations extend to third-party apps and vendors. Three distinct entry paths are mapped, all leveraging legitimate integration permissions that Salesforce customers have already granted. The technique is invisible to detection systems looking for platform exploits.


If your organization uses Salesforce with OAuth-connected third-party apps — which is nearly universal — this attack path is live in your environment right now and requires a trust review, not a patch.


Sources: The Hacker News


Pentagon Suspends CMMC Phase 2 — Comprehensive Review of Defense Contractor Cybersecurity Rules Underway


Jul 14, 24:00


The Department of Defense has suspended CMMC Phase 2 implementation and established a new review and reform task force to conduct a comprehensive reassessment of the contractor cybersecurity certification program. The suspension creates immediate uncertainty for defense contractors who have invested in CMMC compliance preparation and for the third-party assessor ecosystem that has built around the program. No timeline for completion of the review has been announced.


Any organization pursuing or maintaining CMMC compliance needs to halt Phase 2 investment decisions until the review concludes — the requirements landscape is actively changing.


Sources: SecurityWeek


148 npm Packages Disguised as Student Proxies Turned Browsers Into DDoS Botnet — Active for Two Weeks


Jul 14, 24:00


JFrog researchers documented a campaign of 148 npm packages posing as school Wi-Fi bypass tools that loaded malicious JavaScript in students' browsers, silently enrolling them in a DDoS botnet. The operators used npm as free hosting for a booby-trapped proxy site rather than targeting developers who install the packages — a novel abuse of the registry as infrastructure. The campaign ran actively for approximately two weeks in May before detection.


Using npm as hosting infrastructure to compromise end-users rather than developers is a novel supply chain attack pattern that existing registry security scanning won't catch.


Sources: The Hacker News · Cybersecurity News


AI & Machine Learning


Grok Build CLI Was Uploading Entire Git Repositories — Full Commit History Including Files Explicitly Excluded


Jul 14, 24:00


New analysis of the xAI Grok Build coding CLI incident reveals it was uploading entire Git repositories including full commit history to xAI-controlled Google Cloud Storage, not merely the individual files it accessed during tasks. A researcher intercepted a request from version 0.2.93, cloned the git bundle, and recovered files the agent had been explicitly instructed not to access — meaning the exfiltration violated both user intent and stated scope. This is a significantly more severe data exposure than the initial home directory report suggested.


Any developer who used Grok Build on a codebase with sensitive history, credentials, or IP should treat that repository's contents as potentially exposed — and audit what was uploaded.


Sources: The Hacker News


Anthropic's Tokenizer Efficiency Gap Complicates AI Pricing Comparisons — Costs More Tokens Per Task Than Rivals


Jul 14, 24:00


The Register's analysis finds that Anthropic's Claude tokenizer consumes significantly more tokens per equivalent task than competing models, creating a hidden cost multiplier that makes straight per-token price comparisons misleading. Organizations benchmarking Claude against GPT or Gemini on advertised token rates may be systematically underestimating actual Claude costs in production. The issue is particularly relevant as enterprises report AI sticker shock from real-world deployments.


If you're making Claude vs. competitor cost decisions based on published token prices without accounting for tokenizer efficiency differences, your cost models are wrong.


Sources: The Register


DOGE Deployed AI for Housing Policy — HUD Withheld Records Citing a Privilege That Doesn't Exist


Jul 14, 24:00


Wired reports that in response to a public records request, HUD withheld documents about DOGE's use of AI in housing policy decisions, citing a legal privilege that attorneys say does not exist. The opacity extends to what AI systems were used, how outputs informed policy, and what oversight governed the deployment. The incident raises substantive questions about accountability when AI is used in government decision-making without transparency.


Government use of AI for consequential policy decisions with no transparency or accountability framework is a live governance failure with direct implications for AI regulation debates.


Sources: Wired


US Worker Productivity at Record Highs — Without AI Credit


Jul 14, 24:00


NYT analysis finds US worker productivity is at historically high levels, driven by tight labor markets, digitization, and remote work adoption — with AI not yet registering as a significant contributor in the data. The finding complicates the dominant AI ROI narrative at a moment when enterprises are spending heavily on AI tools and investors are pricing in transformative productivity gains. The gap between AI investment and measurable productivity attribution is becoming a material question for corporate boards.


If productivity records are being set without AI contribution, the burden of proof for AI ROI claims just got higher — relevant for anyone justifying or evaluating AI investment cases.


Sources: NYT Business


China June Exports Surge 27% YoY — AI Boom Driving Strong Demand Cited as Key Factor


Jul 14, 24:00


China's customs agency reported a 27% year-over-year surge in June exports, with AI-driven hardware demand explicitly cited as a significant contributor to the acceleration. The figure aligns with TSMC's 68% revenue surge and reinforces that AI infrastructure buildout is pulling manufacturing capacity at scale. The export data also suggests Chinese suppliers are benefiting substantially from global AI investment despite trade restrictions.


27% export growth with AI explicitly named as a driver is a macro-level confirmation that AI infrastructure demand is reshaping global trade flows — relevant for supply chain and procurement planning.


Sources: Euronews Business


PsiQuantum Reveals Architecture for Massive Photonic Quantum Computer — 100 Cryogenic Cabinets, Light-Based Qubits


Jul 14, 24:00


PsiQuantum has detailed its technical architecture for building a large-scale quantum computer using photonic qubits — encoding quantum information in particles of light rather than superconducting circuits. The system will require approximately 100 cryogenic stainless-steel cabinets cooled near absolute zero, in a form factor resembling a data center. The photonic approach offers potential manufacturing scalability advantages over competing qubit technologies, and the disclosure marks a significant technical transparency moment for a company that has raised over $700M.


A concrete architectural roadmap from one of the best-funded quantum computing companies is a meaningful signal for anyone tracking when fault-tolerant quantum compute becomes a real planning horizon.


Sources: MIT Technology Review


Technology


New York Enacts Nation's First Statewide Data Center Moratorium — Blocks New Permits for Facilities Over 50MW for Up to a Year


Jul 14, 24:00


New York Governor Kathy Hochul signed an executive order imposing a moratorium on new environmental permits for hyperscale data centers exceeding 50 megawatts, making New York the first state to impose such a restriction. The order gives the state up to a year to develop regulations addressing energy price impacts and environmental effects on residents. A separate legislative bill with an even lower 20MW threshold awaits her signature, which could restrict significantly more developments.


The first statewide data center moratorium in the US directly affects AI infrastructure siting decisions and signals a regulatory template other states may follow — a material constraint on where hyperscalers and AI companies can build.

UK Social Media Under-16 Ban Gets Research Backing — Study Confirms Removing Phones Makes Teens 'Act Like Humans Again'


Jul 14, 24:00


UK ministers advancing legislation to ban social media for under-16s have published supporting research confirming behavioral improvements in teens when phone access is removed, with The Register drily noting this is 'the least surprising study of the year.' The research adds political momentum to legislation already advancing through Parliament, with the EU simultaneously moving toward a similar under-13 ban. The convergence of UK and EU regulatory action signals coordinated Western movement on platform age restrictions.


UK and EU legislation converging on social media age restrictions within the same legislative window means platforms face imminent compliance obligations in two of the world's largest markets simultaneously.

Microsoft Tests Windows Search Without Ads — Prioritizes Relevant Results Over Promotional Content

Microsoft has begun testing a redesigned Windows Search experience that removes ads and promotional content, returning the feature to a focus on relevant local and web results. Valarian Raises $50M for Sovereign Infrastructure Control Layer — Total Funding Reaches $70M

UK-based cybersecurity firm Valarian closed a $50 million funding round, bringing total raised to $70 million, for its ACRA sovereign infrastructure control technology. The raise reflects growing European investment in infrastructure sovereignty solutions as geopolitical risk intensifies.

Oil Breaches $85 Per Barrel as US-Iran Gulf Conflict Escalates — Brent at One-Month High

Brent crude crossed $85 per barrel for the first time in a month as US-Iran military exchanges in the Gulf intensify and Strait of Hormuz shipping risk remains elevated. German Manufacturer ZEGO-TVZ Files for Insolvency — Blames 6-Week Production Shutdown from Cyberattack


Jul 13, 24:00


German industrial firm ZEGO-TVZ has filed for insolvency, directly attributing the failure to a March 2026 cyberattack that shut down production for six weeks. The company states it could not recover financially from the extended operational outage caused by the intrusion. The case is a stark data point on the existential business risk of cyberattacks against manufacturing and production environments.


A company going bankrupt because of a cyberattack is the clearest possible illustration of operational cyber risk — directly relevant for any organization assessing cyber resilience and business continuity planning.


Sources: The Register


ModHeader Extension Pulled from Chrome and Edge After Hidden Browsing History Collector Found in 1.6M-Install Build


Jul 13, 24:00


Google and Microsoft removed the ModHeader browser extension — with roughly 1.6 million combined installs across Chrome and Edge — after researchers discovered a dormant browsing history collection mechanism built into the official store version. The collector was switched off via an empty allow-list and no evidence of data exfiltration was found. The incident mirrors a growing pattern of trusted, high-install browser extensions being found with covert data collection capabilities.


A 1.6 million-install extension with a hidden data collector underscores why browser extension vetting needs to be part of enterprise endpoint policy — the attack surface is enormous and largely unmonitored.


Sources: The Hacker News


US Treasury Sanctions VPN Service Used by Ransomware Groups — First VPN Provider Sanctioned


Jul 13, 24:00


The US Treasury Department sanctioned First VPN Service (1VPNS) and its Ukrainian administrator for knowingly providing anonymization infrastructure to ransomware groups, marking the first time a VPN provider has been targeted with US sanctions for facilitating cybercrime. A separate sanction was issued against a Belarusian man for operating malware cryptor services. The actions signal Treasury is expanding its sanctions toolkit upstream into criminal infrastructure enablers.


Sanctioning a VPN provider for ransomware facilitation sets a new precedent for how the US government targets cybercriminal infrastructure — a signal for compliance teams tracking sanctions exposure in the security tools supply chain.


Sources: The Record


CrashStealer macOS Malware Uses Notarized Dropper to Bypass Gatekeeper — Steals Keychain, Credentials, Crypto


Jul 13, 24:00


Jamf Threat Labs disclosed CrashStealer, a new macOS infostealer written in native C++ that impersonates Apple's crash reporting tool to steal credentials, keychain data, and cryptocurrency wallets. Critically, the dropper is notarized by Apple — meaning it passes Gatekeeper checks — making it significantly harder for users to identify as malicious. The native C++ implementation also makes it harder to detect than AppleScript or Objective-C-based stealers.


A notarized macOS infostealer that impersonates a trusted Apple system tool and bypasses Gatekeeper is a high-sophistication threat to any Mac-heavy enterprise environment.

Apple's trade secrets lawsuit against OpenAI alleges that employees who departed for OpenAI (and Jony Ive's IO Products, acquired by OpenAI) took confidential hardware and AI secrets, with some allegedly coached on how to avoid triggering Apple's data loss detection systems. One former employee allegedly exploited a 'rare' bug to download sensitive files from Apple's network long after his departure. NYT reports that the Trump administration's recent scrutiny of AI models — including reviews of frontier labs — may be a prelude to demanding ownership stakes in leading AI companies, following the pattern of the administration taking equity positions in other strategic private companies. PixVerse, a video generation AI startup, has closed a $439 million funding round valuing the company above $2 billion. The raise is one of the largest in the AI video generation space, which is seeing rapid investment as the technology approaches commercial production quality.

Nous Research (Hermes AI Agent Maker) in Talks for $75M+ at $1.5B Valuation


Jul 13, 24:00


Nous Research, the company behind the Hermes family of open-source AI agents, is in fundraising discussions targeting at least $75 million at a $1.5 billion valuation, led by Robot Ventures with significant participation from USV. Andrew Kelley, creator of the Zig programming language, publicly criticized the Bun JavaScript runtime's decision to rewrite a component in Rust using Claude AI assistance, calling the output 'unreviewed slop.' The controversy cuts to a central debate in software engineering: whether AI-generated code that works but wasn't deeply reviewed represents acceptable technical debt.


The Bun/Zig controversy is crystallizing the debate about AI-assisted code quality standards — a question every engineering org deploying AI coding tools needs to have a policy answer to.

Apple iOS 27, macOS 27 Golden Gate, and watchOS 27 Public Betas Launch — Siri AI Finally Works


Jul 13, 24:00


Apple released public betas for iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27 Golden Gate, and watchOS 27, making the revamped Siri AI available to a broad audience for the first time. EU Social Media Under-13 Ban Moving to Legislation — Von der Leyen Signals Timeline of Months

An expert panel recommended platforms be required to prove their services are not harmful to minors before gaining access to them. OnePlus and parent company Oppo are reportedly set to announce in the coming days a withdrawal from US and European consumer markets, according to a WinFuture report. General Fusion began trading on the Nasdaq following a reverse merger, becoming the first publicly traded commercial fusion energy company. Ghostcommit: PNG-Embedded Prompt Injection Bypasses AI Code Reviewers, Exfiltrates Repo Secrets


Jul 11, 24:00


Researchers demonstrated 'Ghostcommit,' a technique that hides prompt injection instructions inside PNG image files committed to repositories. AI code review tools CodeRabbit and Bugbot never open image files, so the injection goes undetected — then convinces a coding agent to read the repo's .env file and encode every secret into the codebase as a list of numbers. The attack requires no special privileges and exploits a fundamental blind spot in how AI agents handle non-text file types.


Any team using AI coding agents for code review or automation has a new, undefended exfiltration path that bypasses current tooling — secrets are at risk from a committed image file.


Sources: BleepingComputer
